## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Visālakkhivimānavatthu* ("Mansion of the Beautiful-Eyed Goddess", Vv 37) is a canonical verse narrative located in the *Vimānavatthu* of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The work illustrates how keeping the moral precepts, living a restrained life, practicing generosity, and maintaining faith yield celestial happiness and high rebirth [SuttaCentral]. In his commentary on the *Visālakkhivimāna* story (*Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* 169–172), Dhammapāla examines the distinction between performing a virtuous deed and its eventual "ripening" (*vipāka*) in a later existence, focusing on the verse declaration that one's former virtue had not yet ripened (*yañ ca sīlavatī āsiṁ na taṁ tāva vipaccati*) [Monius 2001].
The DharmaNexus database identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse across 11 texts (90 matching passages), with no cross-language matches meeting threshold criteria [DharmaNexus]. Beyond its commentary (*Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, matching §4.1–14.4), the text exhibits substantial formulaic overlap with the *Nimijātaka* (Ja 541, §6.1–8.3) and its commentary [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, recurring verse segments are shared with several other *Vimānavatthu* accounts—including *Uttarāvimānavatthu* (Vv 15), *Lakhumāvimānavatthu* (Vv 19), *Bhadditthivimānavatthu* (Vv 22), *Soṇadinnāvimānavatthu* (Vv 23), *Uposathāvimānavatthu* (Vv 24), and *Niddāvimānavatthu* (Vv 25)—as well as the *Catumahārājasutta* (AN 3.37) and the *Sānusutta* (SN 10.5) [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also notes contextual links to the *Surucijātaka* (Ja 489), *Revatīvimānavatthu* (Vv 52), *Revatīpetavatthu* (Pv 39), and *Mittātherīgāthā* (Thig 2.7) [SuttaCentral].
